events.name: Album Listening: Mother by Cleo Sol
Majlis x Cinenova
events.description:
A Programme of Shorts from the Cinenova Collection



We’re collaborating with the feminist film distributor Cinenova on a special programme of shorts drawn from their collection of over 300 works made between 1910s and early 2000s.



The event is programmed by Reman Sadani, Omoyemi Akintab and Siufan Adey, with support from the Cinenova Working Group. The screening will be followed by a discussion around working with film collections.



******************** Full programme ********************



Memory Tracks (1997) by Jamika Ajalon – 8 minsA tribute to African-American women activists, whose violent actions were often characterised as being the result of mental illness.



Stranger Baby (1995) by Lana Lin – 14 mins

Framed as a mock science fiction, Stranger Baby offers different perspectives on what it means to be human and what is labeled ‘alien’.



B.U.C.K.L.E. (1994) by Julie Tolentino and Catherine Gund – 11 mins

A humorous fast-paced parody of women dancing, cruising and picking up women at New York City's legendary Clit Club. (Please note: there is a brief moment of sexualised nudity in the film.)



Back Inside Herself (1984) by S. Pearl Sharp – 4 mins

Described by the artist as ‘a visual poem on identity’, Back Inside Herself shows a Black woman finding her own sense of self and rejecting hegemonic societal expectations of who she should be and how she should behave.



******************** Schedule ********************



18:30 - Doors Open



19.00 - Intro + Screening



19.45 - Break



20.00 - Discussion



21.00 - End

................



Founded in 1991, following the merger of Circles and Cinema of Women (two feminist film and video distributors each established in 1979), Cinenova has continued to care for and distribute the work of radical artists and collectives, who have documented important social movements and engaged critically with gender, race, sexuality, health, work and community.

................

Majlis is our regular film club taking place every second Monday of the month. It’s a manifestation of our collective intention to continue our deep dive into films, expand on forms of political education and create a space where our community can gather, sit together, and converse about common issues over a shared meal or drink. The film club is open to all to attend, but prioritises Black and non-white cultural/film workers

................

Other Cinemas is a project focused on the transformational power of film; whether tthat is showcasing the work of Black and non-white filmmakers; creating networks for Black and non-white creatives to work, learn and collaborate; or using film to document the stories of Black and non-white communities. Other Cinemas regularly hosts free film screenings in ways and spaces that serve our communities and also runs an informal film school collective of young Black and non-white filmmakers which seeks to create a real space for conversation and collaboration. Other Cinemas was set up by Arwa Aburawa and Turab Shah, two filmmakers who saw the need for better ways to make and share films.

events.name: Performance: Ewa Poniatowska
events.description:
Join us for a performance exploring the hidden infrastructures and informal economies of communist Poland, accompanying Monika Sosnowska’s current exhibition Weight of Matter.

We were too poor to spend our vacation in the country, is a new performance by Ewa Poniatowska exploring borders, smuggling and Polish commercial tourism in the 1970s-1990s. The work stems from her research into black markets and the history of underground commerce in communist countries. Featuring a musical score by Ewa, and performed with Kazumi Nishimura.
 

ARTIST BIOS

Ewa Poniatowska is a Polish artist based in London. Her practice spans across visual art, performance and music, often playing with symbols of desire and facades of luxury. Poniatowska is also the co-founder of RSVP, a nomadic platform for performance and live-art and one half of an experimental music and performance duo Rat Section. 
 
Kazumi Nishimura is a Japanese artist and performer based in London. Her practice brings together dance, food, and visual expression, drawing on her experience as a dancer, and private dining chef. Through her work with nyotaimori, she explores ritual and intimacy from a female perspective, considering the body as both a medium of expression and a site of encounter. 

ACCESS

Event is not seated, and some areas have uneven flooring, which may affect wheelchair access.

events.description:
SET presents a programme of five films exploring the surreal, the silly and the unexpected. Playing with performance and improvisation, they oscillate between the everyday and the existential, finding humour in situations where the plot unravels and nothing goes quite to plan.



Featuring a weird cig break; best friends on a shoplifting spree; a strangely romantic fishing trip-cum-stag do; and an extra wandering around a replica set of the American Museum of Natural History, they are best watched with an appreciation for the absurd.



Doors open at 6.45pm. The screening will begin promptly at 7.30pm and will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers, hosted by Ellie Dobbs.

events.description:
🚨 LONDON, FROM THE MARGINS: BRICK BY BRICK — FULL LINEUP & SCHEDULE DROP 🚨

On Sat 14 Nov, we’re bringing together the voices, sounds and people pushing Grime forward. From the spaces that built the culture to the next generation ready to carry it, we’re celebrating the scene brick by brick.

Film, conversation, cyphers and live sets. The full lineup is locked, the schedule is set, and now you know what’s going down. 👀💥

HERE’S THE FULL RUN-DOWN ⬇️

🎬 FILM SCREENING – 6.30PM
THE DANCE BEGINS AT HOME
We kick things off with an exclusive screening of @jessebern.ard's The Dance Begins at Home, exploring the people, places and energy at the heart of Grime.

🗣️ PANEL TALK – 7.30PM
NO LICENSE
Who builds the spaces that keep Grime alive? And how do we make sure they’re here for the next generation? @jessebern.ard leads a panel discussion, joined by M.I.C of @travspresents, Shakira Wallace and @shivzstar of @beam.ig to get into the realities of building, sustaining and passing on Grime culture.

🔊 LIVE MUSIC — 8.30PM–3AM

events.name: Basket of Light
events.description:
Basket of Light is coming to London for a free day party organised by Barnet Council on 15 November!

It’s a strange and beautiful lakeside space which @barnetcouncil has taken over for a weekend to support the importance of light. We’re so chuffed to be invite to help the celebrations, and bring a brief flicker of our summer dance to London in the deep heart of Autumn.

We have programmed 5 hours of boundary pushing performances using sound and light - from incendiary vocal trio @alkanna.graeca to AV experiments with @visuals_ru and @sonic_seed, using found audio and imagery from across the borough. All with the support of guest selectors @graceeee.ems and @swayoftheverses and our resident DJs Tambourine Hands.

Light + Flight is presented by Art in Barnet. It’s fully funded by external sources - including a cultural impact award, part of the Mayor’s London Borough of Culture Programme, with additional support from the National Heritage Lottery Fund and Arts Council England.
